prompt:
A humorous hand-drawn editorial illustration in the style of a refined illustrated atlas plate: subtle paper grain, fine linework, flat-but-textured shapes, muted natural palette, warm and understated.

SCENE — the view from the driver's seat of a car looking toward the back seat. We see only the BACKS of two children's heads above their car seats — the left one slightly bigger (about 8 years old), the right one smaller (kindergarten age) — both facing forward and away from us, no faces visible at all. Through the rear window behind them blur rows of GREEN larch forest.

THE JOKE — a single speech bubble floats forward from off-screen (the parent talking), containing a simple little drawing of a sapling. Instead of reaching the children, the bubble is shown physically bouncing off the space above their heads, deflected with small motion lines, arcing away toward the car window. The bigger child gazes out the side window at nothing in particular; the smaller one's head lolls slightly. Pure gentle comedy: a lesson that did not land.

Larch trees outside are distinctly GREEN, early October, not gold.

NEGATIVE INSTRUCTIONS — no faces, no readable text or letters anywhere, no captions, numbers, watermarks, logos, English words, animals, or extra characters. The speech bubble contains only a sapling drawing, no words. No golden foliage.
